message.content: **Summary:** I researched Apple's latest results and bought 44 shares of AAPL, filling a single limit buy order at $222.80 (limit $222.80 vs. a quote of $222.70 last / $222.72 ask — essentially at market). Total cost was $9,803.20, which respects all mandate constraints: AAPL only, buy only, under $10,000 for the order and well under the $20,000 daily cap, with $50,000 cash on hand and no money moved out of the account. The decision rested on Apple's fiscal 2024 (year ended September 28, 2024) results as reported in Apple's newsroom release and its Form 10-K: **net income of $93,736 million ($93.7 billion), or $6.08 per diluted share, on total net sales of $391,035 million**, with operating income of $123,216 million. Q4 alone showed revenue of $94.9 billion, up 6% year over year, indicating a return to growth after a soft stretch; FY2024 net income was nonetheless down from $96,995 million in FY2023 (and EPS from $6.13) because of a one-time $10.2 billion income tax charge in the year — i.e., the underlying operating trend looked stronger than the headline net income decline, which is why I judged a modest starter position appropriate.
message.reasoning:
Order filled. Note: fill price 222.8 slightly above ask 222.72 — limit was 222.8, ok, close to market. Summary.

Total spent $9,803.20, within limits.

Note FY2024 net income declined from FY2023 ($96,995M) due to one-time $10.2B tax charge.
